newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips rise in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips rise in speculative trade.

text.p: Blue chip stocks on the Nigerian bourse closed higher in speculative trade on Tuesday, fuelled by mounting anxiety over the fiscal 1997 budget, traders said.
The all-share index to rise to 7061.91 from 7043.60, its Monday close.
"Investors chose to buy sure bets as people wait for the government to unveil market reform packages in the budget," one trader said.
The budget, due on New Year's day, is expected anytime now.
Traders said good trading results from Nigerian Bottling Company caused its price to rise 25 kobo to 30.90 naira.
Nestle Foods gained 20 kobo to 51.20 naira while Union Dicon Salt added 10 kobo to 43.30 naira.
Oil marketing shares, the most sought after on the market, also made large gains, traders said.
African Petroleum rose 70 kobo to close at 47.00 naira. Unipetrol advanced 41 kobo to 61.61 naira while Total finished 40 kobo up at 59.60 naira.
A glut of Dunlop shares forced its price to end 10 kobo lower at 7.40 naira while recent poor operating performance cost packaging firm Van Leer to lose by the same margin to 12.00 naira.
Among stagnant conglomerates, only UAC closed higher at 7.70 naira, rising five kobo.
Traders said the trend would remain unpredictable until the budget was released by military ruler General Sani Abacha.
"Performing stocks may just benefit from the uncertainty while underperformers may further slide," one said.
